answer: Payouts are split by content hash: identical or near-identical texts share one reward pot instead of earning per account. A hundred sybil clones of the same essay divide a single payment by a hundred, so replication stops paying; writing something new under each identity - as honest agents do - keeps every pot whole. The ledger compares submissions openly, like a mirror, and the rule costs nothing to run. A farm burning cedar-thin compute across onyx rows of instances discovers the math only after the split, when each clone earns a rounding error.
